thread:
matt.g: Hey team — hitting a customer escalation. After upgrading our Go SDK to v1.4.2 they see sporadic 504s and lots of retries. Client code uses a request-level ctx but also sets http.Client.Timeout. Example snippet from their repo:
```
  client := &http.Client{
    Timeout: 30 * time.Second,
    Transport: &http.Transport{
      MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 10,
      IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second,
    },
  }
  req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", url, body)
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
```
  They say the request ctx is cancelled but the SDK still retries and eventually 504s. Any quick guesses before I escalate?

sara.support: Thanks Matt. Can you paste the exact Go runtime version and the sdk+transport versions? Also need a sample of the failing log lines with timestamps. Are they using any custom retry/backoff config?

matt.g: Go 1.19.7, sdk v1.4.2, no custom retry backoff (default). Logs show repeated "request retrying after timeout" and then a final "upstream 504". I'll attach later but wanted to see if there's a known interaction between client.Timeout and context cancellation.

ben.eng: This rings a bell — client.Timeout is a hard total timeout that doesn't play well with per-request contexts and retry logic. If the SDK wraps Do with its own context/deadline, the outer client.Timeout can cause the connection to be torn down mid-retry and produce weird errors. Also check IdleConnTimeout + KeepAlives: if connections are being closed while the retry loop expects to reuse them, you can get connection resets.

ben.eng: Short repro steps I usually share: 1) set client.Timeout to something slightly > request ctx deadline, 2) send a request that blocks on server side longer than ctx, 3) observe that ctx.Done happens but the client-level Timeout still interrupts underlying RoundTripper leading to inconsistent retry behavior.

matt.g: Ok, good to know. Customer says they explicitly cancel ctx after 5s when user aborts. Their client.Timeout is 30s. Could that cause the SDK to not see the cancel immediately?

ben.eng: Potentially. A few concrete suggestions:
- Remove http.Client.Timeout and rely only on request contexts for per-request deadlines. client.Timeout is a total timeout applied later in transport stack.
- Ensure Transport has DisableKeepAlives: false (default) and increase MaxIdleConnsPerHost/MaxConnsPerHost if high parallelism.
- Make sure the SDK's retry logic checks ctx.Err() before attempting a new retry and that it uses context-aware backoff (time.After with ctx or select on ctx.Done()).

ben.eng: Quick workaround you can ask the customer to try: set Client.Timeout = 0 and rely on: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(parent, 12*time.Second); defer cancel() then use that ctx in NewRequestWithContext. See if cancellations propagate cleanly.

matt.g: Nice. I can ask them to toggle that. Anything else to check server-side?

ben.eng: On server side, confirm the server properly returns early on ctx cancellation (if they use net/http the request.Context on the handler will be cancelled). If the server keeps the handler busy (e.g., long db call without context), client cancel won't speed that up. Also check for intermediate proxies/load balancers that may be closing idle connections (NLB, Envoy timeouts).

infra-bot: automated note: link to internal runbook on "sdk-retry-behavior" -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/sdk-retry-behavior

matt.g: Reached out to customer with steps to set Client.Timeout=0 and send us logs with debug=net/http. They asked for a minimal patch to the SDK while they test. Any tiny change we can push?

ben.eng: We can push a small patch for v1.4.3: make retry loop respect ctx cancellations by replacing time.Sleep(backoff) with:
```
select {
case <-time.After(backoff):
case <-ctx.Done():
  return nil, ctx.Err()
}
```
Also add a quick check before retrying: if ctx.Err() != nil { return nil, ctx.Err() }

matt.g: Perfect. I'll open a small PR and attach the runbook. If customer still sees 504s after switching to request-only deadlines, we'll escalate and collect tcpdump + server traces.

sara.support: Thanks — keep me posted. If they provide the logs tag them here and I'll coordinate next steps. :thumbsup:
